svg.title: Infant choking and collapse action card
svg.desc: Working Australian choking card for an infant under one year, followed by the collapse branch for any age. If the infant is coughing effectively and breathing, let the infant cough, watch continuously and do not strike. For a weak or silent cough or little air, call Triple Zero. Support the responsive infant face-down and head-low for up to five back blows, then face-up and head-low for up to five two-finger chest thrusts on the lower half of the breastbone, checking after each action. The actions are the same with or without a first-aid kit and equipment must not delay treatment. If anyone becomes unresponsive, remove only a clearly visible object. Start CPR only if unresponsive and not breathing normally; otherwise use the side position and keep watching. Abdominal thrusts, blind finger sweeps, shaking and inversion are prohibited.
svg.text: CHOKING — INFANT UNDER 1 YEAR
Plus the collapse branch for any age
WARNING — HANDS-ON REVIEW OUTSTANDING
Subjective estimates: source match 95%; new illustration 60%.
These are not safety, treatment-success or survival probabilities.
Infant support and hand positions need paediatric first-aid review.
Follow the 000 call-taker. This is not a substitute for training.
Adult or child age 1+ and still responsive? Use Card 1.
CAN THE INFANT COUGH EFFECTIVELY?
YES — let the infant cough. Watch continuously.
Do not strike or shake.
WEAK / SILENT OR LITTLE AIR? Call 000 now.
Start Step 1 only while the infant is responsive.
FACE-DOWN, HEAD LOWER — BACK BLOWS
Support the infant across your forearm or lap.
Support the head, jaw and shoulders.
Do not press the soft throat.
Give up to 5 sharp blows between the shoulder blades.
Check after every blow. Stop as soon as the object clears.
FACE-UP, HEAD LOWER — CHEST THRUSTS
Turn the infant while supporting the head and body.
Keep the infant face-up and head lower across your thigh.
Use 2 fingers on the lower half of the breastbone.
Give up to 5 chest thrusts. Check after each; stop if clear.
STILL BLOCKED AND RESPONSIVE?
Alternate the two steps. Check after every action.
No abdominal thrusts. Do not shake or hold upside down.
Kit or no kit: use the same actions.
Do not delay to fetch equipment.
ANY AGE: PERSON BECOMES UNRESPONSIVE
1. Open and check the airway.
2. Remove an object only if it is clearly visible.
Never sweep blindly with a finger.
3. Not breathing normally, gasping or unsure?
Call 000; firm surface; start CPR; attach an AED.
4. Breathing normally? Use the side position and keep watching.
Use the guide’s CPR, AED and recovery-position cards.
AFTER IT CLEARS
Stop blows and thrusts. Keep watching breathing.
If 000 has been called, update the call-taker.
Persistent cough, wheeze, noisy or difficult breathing,
coughing blood or fever needs medical assessment.
WORKING DRAFT — infant/collapse card; use with Card 1 and follow 000
